draft.title: Strata and community living
card: In a strata scheme, each person owns their own unit (a lot). They also share ownership of the common property, such as lifts, stairs, gardens and the roof.
the body made up of all the lot owners. It manages and maintains the common property and makes decisions for the scheme.
the rules for the scheme, such as limits on noise, pets or parking. They bind owners and occupiers, including tenants.
Strata law in NSW, including the Strata Schemes Management Act 2015 (NSW), sets out how schemes run. Owners usually pay levies to cover the costs of common property.
draft.remember: Own your lot, share the common property, and follow the rules the owners corporation sets within strata law.

a.q: In a NSW strata scheme, who is responsible for managing and maintaining the common property?
opts: The owners corporation
Each tenant in the building
The local council
The owner of the top floor lot
a.why: The owners corporation is made up of all lot owners and manages the common property for the whole scheme. Tenants are tempting, but they do not own lots and so are not part of the owners corporation.
a.clue: Think of the body made up of every lot owner.

b.q: Priya rents a unit in a NSW strata building. The scheme's by-laws ban keeping a dog. Priya's lease says nothing about pets. Can the by-laws apply to her?
opts: Yes, by-laws bind tenants as well as owners
No, by-laws bind only the owners of lots
No, because her lease does not mention pets
Yes, but only if the council approves the by-law
b.why: By-laws bind everyone who lives in the scheme, including tenants, so the dog ban can apply to Priya. It does not matter that the lease is silent, because the by-laws are a separate set of rules for the scheme.
b.clue: Check who the by-laws bind besides owners.

b.best: Yes, by-laws bind tenants as well as owners

problems.detail: The scenario uses a by-law that bans keeping a dog. In NSW, Cooper v The Owners – Strata Plan No 58068 [2020] NSWCA 250 held that a blanket animal ban was invalid. Since 2021, s 137B of the Strata Schemes Management Act 2015 (NSW) says a by-law has no force to the extent it unreasonably prohibits keeping an animal. So students may learn that a blanket dog ban validly applies to Priya. The question should use an enforceable by-law instead, such as noise or parking.
The clue 'Think of the body made up of every lot owner' restates the card's definition of the owners corporation, which gives the answer away.
